title: Commuting Division-Coefficient Forms and the Artinian Eisenbud--Green--Harris Conjecture
main_claim: EGH holds over every characteristic-zero field for homogeneous regular sequences with all degrees >= 2. The proof constructs commuting linear forms t_i with central-division-algebra coefficients that satisfy triangular power identities t_i^{a_i} = c_i f_i + sum B f_l + sum C t_d. These give an ordered left-Delta basis of Delta[x], and least exponents then yield a monomial ideal containing the pure powers with the same Hilbert function. The non-Artinian and general-field cases follow from the Caviglia–Maclagan reduction and descent.

issues.location: Sec. 6, Lemma determinant-descent (genuine H-equivariance of F⊗D)
issues.description: The cancellation of the scalar cocycle is argued only through weights: F has weight 1 in A, and the determinant correction D has weights (-1,0). The group-law compatibility is asserted via 'functoriality of determinants' without an explicit cocycle computation. This step is the crux for e_1 | r, so the division property depends on it. I believe it holds; it is just stated very tersely.
issues.evidence: 'Functoriality of determinants and the genuine transport of the original module identify the two maps for these composed choices. ... Thus no scalar cocycle remains, and the maps glue to genuine equivariance.'

coverage:
Read all of §§1–9 in LaTeX. Checked the following:
- §2: the ordered-basis lemma (CM/s.o.p. argument, Hilbert count) and monomial extraction (least exponents are translation-invariant under right multiplication by t_j; a_i e_i is the least exponent because every C_id t_d term has a positive coordinate d > i; N/ΔI ≅ Δ⊗S/I).
- §3: the differential-operator annihilator equation, the lowest-order term r(r-1)p^{r-2}h q(∇p), the gradient-curve degree bound b(b-1) ≤ D, the logarithmic-derivative step and the pure-power/base-point contradiction; the initial Clifford-type division algebra (center = k because v_0 is even; s_ρ^2 = q_ρ); the squareclass degree bound; sparsity preservation.
- §4: the defective-Jacobian dimension bound, which gives codim Sing ≥ M-2s+1; the join connectivity of 2M-2; the compact-support Leray degree bookkeeping; the duality transfers; the inequalities κ ≤ 2M-4s and 2s+κ-1 ≤ 2M-2 from M ≥ 2h+4s+10; the π_1 argument.
- §5: the Kummer degree b^{b-1}; branch points; T_0 has valuations (1,1,-1,-1) and genus b-1; the Abhyankar étaleness; deg L = b^b; the generic degree-(g-1) vanishing giving a trivial pushforward; the matrix transport law; freeness on Pic^1; the character maps.
- §6–7: the reduced-rank bookkeeping (dim e_0 r); the mixed Picard pairing ±rank; the torsor Euler lemma; the e_0^2 e_1 divisibility; the obstruction-theory dimensions (M+2h and 2h+1); the integral K-pushforward giving q_j ∈ e_1 Z; the Hilbert-series and Koszul step; the p-adic truncation lemma (verified the induction by hand); the order ν = s(p^a - 1).
- §8: the Veronese finite-extension identities (u_T, z formulas, v^b = z^b - u^b); weight bookkeeping λ_{m-1} = λ_m χ_m with λ_M = 1; commutativity of new forms with old ones; the nonzero f_i coefficient via integrality of X.
- §9: the use of CM08 Prop. 10 and field descent.

Not independently verified: the cited external results themselves (Hamm–Lê Lefschetz, CM08 Prop. 10, Caviglia–Sbarra).
